newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah soft, swaps jump.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah soft, swaps jump.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah remained soft against the dollar at mid-morning on Thursday while swap points jumped on offshore buying, dealers said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,439.0/40.0 at 0235 GMT after finding some support at the 2,439.0 level, compared with an opening of 2,433.0/44.0.
Swap rates rose broadly on foreign buying, dealers said.
They said a carry-forward effect from Wednesday, coupled with the ongoing jitters in the Thai market, hit the rupiah which again triggered off stop-loss dollar buying.

The rupiah tumbled to a low 2,445 in London overnight on false rumours of violence and arson at a police station in Jakarta, but recovered later to 2,435. Dealers said stop-loss limits were triggered in Singapore and London late on Wednesday after the rupiah hit by the false rumours.
One major local bank dealer said swap points jumped in early Thursday trading as offshore operators were squeezed on the forward side.
"Offshore players going long on dollars have to buy swaps for hedging or to get the rupiah financing, driving swap rates up across the board," the dealer said.
One-week swaps rose to 5.0/6.0, one-month to 19.0/19.5, two to 29.5/32.0, three to 48.5/49.0 and six to 88.0/90.0.
Dealers said jitters in the rupiah was also partly due to a spill-over from foreign attacks on the Thai baht.
They said a relatively ample money market, with overnight money traded at 10.5/11.5 percent, was also helpful for dollar purchases.
